hyps.why: At already large learning rates, further increases push Adam into divergence or unstable training.
Tiny learning rates leave the network undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them gives large gains.
Reducing an unstable, too-large learning rate restores convergence.
Lowering an already tiny learning rate deepens undertraining.
Small batches already have noisy gradients, so larger steps destabilize training more.
With a tiny learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and worse undertraining.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise that compounds instability at high learning rates.
Strong L2 penalties near 1 cause underfitting, so increasing them further hurts much more.
At negligible alpha values a step up changes almost nothing, unlike in the range where it starts hurting.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to unstable training at large step sizes.
